question: What is the primary structural change in red blood cells during a sickle cell crisis?

options.A: Cells turn into rigid crescent shapes
options.B: Cells shrink into tiny star-like fragments
options.C: Cells swell into large circular spheres
options.D: Cells lengthen into thin thread-like strands

explanation: Abnormal hemoglobin S forms rigid fibers under low oxygen that distort the flexible red blood cell into a crescent shape. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h1)

question: Why does chronic hemolytic anaemia develop in patients with sickle cell disease?

options.A: Kidneys filter out normal hemoglobin along with excess waste products
options.B: Sickled cells have a much shorter lifespan than normal cells
options.C: The spleen destroys all healthy white blood cells by mistake
options.D: The bone marrow completely stops producing any new blood cells

explanation: Fragile sickle cells break down prematurely in circulation, living only 10 to 20 days instead of the normal 120 days. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h1)

question: What genetic term describes someone who inherits only one sickle cell gene?
explanation: Inheriting a single abnormal gene results in the HbAS genotype, commonly referred to as the sickle cell trait. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h2)

question: What is the chance of two carriers producing a child with sickle cell anaemia?

options.B: One hundred percent chance per pregnancy

explanation: Autosomal recessive inheritance gives a one in four chance for two carrier parents to pass both abnormal genes to a child. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h2)

question: What causes the yellowish discoloration of the sclera in sickle cell anaemia patients?

options.A: Iron deposits building up beneath the surface of the skin
options.B: Blockage of the bile ducts by rigid white blood cells
options.C: Excessive bilirubin released from rapid red blood cell breakdown
options.D: Direct infection of the liver tissues by abnormal hemoglobin

explanation: Rapid destruction of fragile red blood cells floods the bloodstream with bilirubin, leading to visible jaundice. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h3)

question: What is autosplenectomy in patients with long-standing sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: Surgical removal of an enlarged spleen to prevent severe bleeding complications
options.B: Gradual destruction and shrinkage of the spleen from repeated tissue infarcts
options.C: Infection of the spleen requiring emergency intravenous antibiotic treatment
options.D: Sudden swelling of the spleen caused by trapped pooling blood cells

explanation: Repeated small blockages cut off blood supply to the spleen, causing scar tissue buildup and eventual functional loss. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h3)

question: Which type of sickle crisis involves blood pooling rapidly inside the spleen?
explanation: A splenic sequestration crisis happens when large volumes of blood get trapped in the spleen, causing acute enlargement and shock. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h4)

question: What is the primary immediate nursing intervention for a patient experiencing a vaso-occlusive crisis?

options.A: Preparing the patient for immediate surgical removal of the spleen
options.B: Administering prescribed pain relief and intravenous or oral fluids
options.C: Applying cold compresses directly to the painful joints and limbs
options.D: Restricting fluid intake to prevent fluid overload in the lungs

explanation: Reversing dehydration helps thin the blood and reduce sickling, while analgesics control the severe ischemic pain. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h4)

question: What is the gold standard diagnostic test used to confirm sickle cell disease?
explanation: Hemoglobin electrophoresis identifies the exact types and proportions of hemoglobin present in a blood sample. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h5)

question: Why is a reticulocyte count usually elevated in stable sickle cell anaemia patients?

options.A: Immature red blood cells are released because mature cells are too rigid
options.B: Platelets clump together in large numbers to prevent spontaneous bleeding
options.C: White blood cells multiply quickly to fight off ongoing chronic infections
options.D: The bone marrow works overtime to replace rapidly destroyed red blood cells

explanation: High reticulocyte counts indicate active bone marrow production attempting to keep up with chronic hemolysis. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h5)

question: Which prophylactic medication is routinely given to young children with sickle cell anaemia?
explanation: Daily penicillin prophylaxis protects young children with reduced splenic function from dangerous pneumococcal infections. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h6)

question: Why are vaccinations against specific encapsulated bacteria especially critical for sickle cell patients?

options.A: Constant blood transfusions introduce high amounts of bacterial contaminants
options.B: Vaccines cure the underlying genetic defect causing abnormal hemoglobin production
options.C: Their immune systems are naturally hyperactive and attack foreign vaccines
options.D: Their damaged spleens cannot effectively filter out certain bacteria from blood

explanation: Loss of splenic function impairs the body's primary defense against encapsulated organisms, making vaccines vital. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h6)

question: What environmental factor should patients with sickle cell anaemia be taught to avoid?
explanation: Cold exposure triggers peripheral vasoconstriction and can precipitate a painful vaso-occlusive crisis. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h7)

question: Which instruction is most important when teaching parents how to care for a child with sickle cell disease?

options.A: Restrict physical activity completely to prevent any heart strain
options.B: Encourage frequent fluid intake throughout the day and night
options.C: Administer strong pain killers daily whether pain is present or not
options.D: Avoid all fruits and vegetables containing high levels of vitamin C

explanation: Maintaining optimal hydration keeps blood well-diluted and prevents red blood cells from sickling easily. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h7)

question: What is the term for bone death in the hip joint caused by blocked blood supply?
explanation: Blocked microvascular blood flow to the femoral head leads to bone tissue death known as avascular necrosis. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h8)

question: Why does chronic kidney damage frequently occur in patients with sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: Low oxygen levels in the renal medulla damage delicate filtering structures over time
options.B: Frequent urinary tract infections destroy the outer lining of the renal pelvis
options.C: Excess dietary protein accumulates inside the glomeruli and blocks urine flow
options.D: High blood pressure builds up inside the kidneys due to oversized heart chambers

explanation: The unique low-oxygen environment of the renal medulla promotes sickling and progressive nephron destruction. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h8)
